The neighbors can still reach each other around C, so the total pairwise distance only drops from 82 to 70 and the card reads vitality 12." width="100%"} Node vitality measures the impact of removing a node on graph connectivity, defined as the change in sum of all pairwise shortest path distances: vitality(v) = sum_distances(G) - sum_distances(G - v) By default distances are hop counts found by breadth-first search, so edge weights are ignored; with `weighted=True` they are path costs summed over edge weights. The sum runs over ordered pairs of nodes, so on an undirected graph each pair contributes its distance twice; on a directed graph only pairs connected in the direction of the edges contribute. Only finite distances are summed: if removing the node leaves some pairs unable to reach each other, those pairs simply drop out of `sum_distances(G - v)`, so the result is always finite. This matches `closeness_vitality()`, which computes the same value for every node at once. Higher values indicate more important nodes. Vitality is useful for: - ranking nodes by how much the network's overall reachability depends on them - assessing what is lost if a specific station, server, or person drops out - comparing a handful of candidate nodes without scoring the whole graph The method does not modify the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to score, given as an integer node ID or a string label. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, measure distances by edge weight (each edge's weight, `1.0` when unset; the cheapest of parallel edges is used). Default `False` counts hops. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The vitality score for the node. Higher values indicate more vital nodes. Always finite, even when removing the node disconnects the graph. A graph with a single node gives `0.0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist in the graph, or if `weighted=True` and an edge weight is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Vitality is defined as the drop in the network's total pairwise distance caused by removing a single node: $\mathrm{vit}(v) = W(G) - W(G - v)$, where $W(G) = \sum_{u \ne w} d(u, w)$ is the Wiener index, summed over reachable pairs only. Removing a cut vertex makes some distances infinite; those pairs are left out rather than making the result infinite, so cut vertices tend to score high because many long paths disappear along with them. Because computing $W$ requires an all-pairs shortest-path pass (twice: with and without the node), the cost is $O(V \cdot (V + E))$ per call. To score every node, call `closeness_vitality()` once rather than looping over this method. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5-node path, the middle node has the highest vitality (`36.0`): removing it splits the path in two, and every long distance across the middle drops out of the total: ::: {#462dbb79 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # The middle node: removing it splits the path in two graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[2]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 36.0 ``` ::: ::: An endpoint scores lower (`20.0`), since removing it only shortens the path: ::: {#5f465230 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 20.0 ``` ::: ::: The same pattern shows up in a star graph: the hub lies on every path between leaves, so it outscores any individual leaf (`18.0` versus `10.0`): ::: {#f90bf898 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(4) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]), graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (18.0, 10.0) ``` ::: ::: Node labels work just as well as IDs. On an undirected chain `A - B - C`, removing `B` wipes out all six ordered distances (`1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 2`): ::: {#2a28642a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.get_node_vitality("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 8.0 ``` ::: ::: On the directed version of the same chain, only the three forward pairs are connected, so `B` scores half as much: ::: {#7c50043b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.get_node_vitality("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 4.0 ``` ::: :::
